This page does not show live rates. The starting values are examples based on a mid-market rate of about ₹26.2 per dirham in early October 2026, and provider figures are illustrative. Enter current quotes before you decide.

How the Comparison Works

Rupees received = amount sent × provider's rate
Effective rate = rupees received / (amount sent + fee)
Hidden cost = (amount sent + fee) × mid-market rate − rupees received

Example: You send AED 5,000 when the mid-market rate is ₹26.20. Provider A offers ₹26.05 with an AED 22 fee, so you pay AED 5,022 and your family receives ₹1,30,250, for an effective rate of ₹25.9359. Provider B offers ₹25.80 with no fee, so you pay AED 5,000 and your family receives ₹1,29,000, for an effective rate of ₹25.8000. Provider A is the better value, even with its fee.

How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter the amount you want to send in dirhams
  2. Look up today's mid-market rate on a currency site
  3. Enter the rate and fee from each provider's app, website or branch, including any VAT on the fee
  4. Compare the rupees received and the hidden cost. The best value is highlighted in green

Ask whether the provider's quoted amount is what arrives. The receiving bank may also make a charge, and payment by card may cost more than by bank transfer.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best way to compare remittance services?
Compare the rupees received for the same dirhams paid, on the same day. The rate and the fee must be looked at together, because a "zero fee" transfer can carry a weaker rate. The effective rate above combines the two.
What is the mid-market rate?
It is the midpoint between the rates at which banks buy and sell a currency, and is what you see on most currency charts. Consumers rarely receive it, so the gap between it and your rate is effectively a charge.
Why does this calculator not show live rates?
Rates change through the day and differ by provider, amount and payment method, and we do not take live feeds. Enter the current quotes from each provider's own app or branch just before you send, so that you compare actual offers.
Is the money I send to India taxed?
This depends on who receives it and why, and on your residency status in India. Gifts from certain relatives are generally exempt, while other receipts can be taxable. Check with a tax professional if you are sending large amounts.
When is the best time to send money to India?
No one can reliably predict short-term exchange rates. If you send money regularly, a consistent schedule avoids trying to time the market, and the choice of provider is something you can control.
